title: Scheduler hook for KV compaction budgeting at prefill/decode boundaries
creator: Talia Benson
body:
## Context
We’re adding KV cache compaction to reduce fragmentation and burst-driven tail latency. A recurring failure mode in early prototypes was *scheduler-visible latency spikes* when compaction work lands on the hot path during decode (especially under mixed-length + high churn).

This ticket integrates compaction budgeting into the runtime scheduler so compaction work is:
- predictable (bounded per scheduling loop / per request step)
- aligned with natural boundaries (prefill vs decode) to avoid stalling token generation
- observable and controllable (budgets, kill-switch, metrics)

## Problem statement
Today the scheduler has no explicit “budget gate” for memory maintenance work.
- Compaction worker can opportunistically move pages when fragmentation triggers, but without scheduler awareness it may run during decode steps.
- Decode stalls propagate into p95/p99 (and in practice show up as multi-tenant tail spikes during bursts).

We need a scheduler-level API to:
1) allocate a small compaction budget at safe times
2) strictly disallow compaction past the budget once decode is in progress (unless we are in a degraded/overload path where we’re already shedding)

## Proposal (implementation)
### 1) Add a scheduler-owned compaction budget object
- Budget is represented in both:
  - `max_bytes_to_move` (hard cap)
  - `max_time_us` (optional secondary cap to prevent long copy loops)
- Budget resets at deterministic points in the scheduler loop.

### 2) Enforce budgets at prefill/decode boundaries
Hook points:
- **End of prefill batch (preferred):** after we finish prefill compute and before we enqueue decode steps for newly admitted sequences.
- **Between decode micro-batches:** only allow extremely small “maintenance slice” if the scheduler is idle waiting for kernels / if there is slack; default = 0 for Hosted.

Default behavior by phase:
- Prefill phase: allow compaction with configured budget.
- Decode phase: disallow compaction by default; only allow if `allow_decode_compaction=true` *and* scheduler reports slack *and* overall queue depth is below a threshold.

### 3) Budget source + config knobs
Budget parameters come from runtime config (feature-flagged):
- `kv_compaction.enabled`
- `kv_compaction.budget.prefill_bytes`
- `kv_compaction.budget.prefill_time_us`
- `kv_compaction.budget.decode_bytes` (default 0)
- `kv_compaction.budget.decode_time_us` (default 0)
- `kv_compaction.scheduler.max_budget_per_loop_bytes` (guardrail)

### 4) Backpressure integration (minimal for this ticket)
If allocator is in “near-OOM / high fragmentation emergency” state, scheduler should:
- surface a reason code in logs/metrics (e.g., `compaction_emergency=true`)
- optionally trigger eviction path (not implemented here; see ENG-4825)

### 5) Observability requirements
Emit (or ensure emitted) metrics tagged by phase:
- `kv_compaction_budget_bytes_total{phase=prefill|decode}`
- `kv_compaction_bytes_moved_total{phase=...}`
- `kv_compaction_budget_exhausted_total{phase=...}`
- `kv_compaction_time_us_total{phase=...}`

Add trace spans around budgeted compaction sections (if tracing already exists, ensure phase tag is included).

## Acceptance criteria
- No compaction work runs during decode by default (Hosted defaults), verified via counters/spans.
- Under mixed-length burst scenario (perf-canary), p99 regression is <= 1% vs baseline with compaction disabled, while fragmentation improvements are still observed over a multi-minute run.
- Budget enforcement is strict: bytes moved never exceed budget + small constant overhead (accounting for page granularity).
- Kill-switch / config can disable scheduler-triggered compaction without restart.

## Testing plan
- Unit tests:
  - budget accounting (bytes/time caps)
  - phase gating correctness (prefill allowed, decode blocked)
- Integration tests:
  - long-lived sequences + churn: ensure decode remains stable, budgeted compaction executes only at prefill boundaries
  - cancellation during relocation should not deadlock scheduler (edge case tracked separately; see follow-ups)
- Perf validation:
  - run benchmark-lab mixed-length generator and perf-canary scenario; compare p95/p99 + throughput

## Risks / gotchas
- Prefill boundary might be too late if fragmentation spikes mid-decode (emergency path). We should ensure emergency signals are visible even if we choose not to compact in decode.
- If prefill batches are rare (steady decode), compaction may make slower progress; may require background compaction later, but still budgeted.

## Scope
IN SCOPE:
- scheduler hooks + budget object + phase gating
- config wiring for budgets
- metrics / spans necessary to prove gating

OUT OF SCOPE:
- eviction selection logic (ENG-4825)
- UI in Console

## Rollout notes
- Start with internal canary pools with conservative budgets.
- Hosted: decode budgets remain 0 until SRE sign-off.
- Dedicated: may allow small decode budgets only after data shows no tail regression.

## Definition of done
- PR merged with tests
- Perf runs attached in comments
- Default config agreed with SRE/PM for runtime-1.22 canary
comments: 2026-01-14 — Sofia Ivanova: Drafted scheduler hook points. Strong preference: run compaction slice only at end-of-prefill. Decode gating will default to hard off. Need input from Omar on whether compaction progress is acceptable when prefill is low-frequency.

2026-01-16 — Omar El-Sayed: Agree with end-of-prefill as primary hook. For long-lived decode-only workloads we may not make progress; that’s acceptable for v1 as long as fragmentation doesn’t worsen. Please emit a metric for “compaction starvation” (budget offered but 0 opportunities) so we can see this in prod.

2026-01-18 — Sean Gallagher: For Hosted rollout, decode compaction must be 0 by default. Guardrail: if `kv_compaction_bytes_moved` correlates with p99 spikes during canary, we need quick kill-switch. Please make budget gating visible in traces (phase tag is enough).

2026-01-23 — Julian Moore: Scheduler loop already has a natural prefill->decode transition; added callback seems straightforward. Watch out: prefill can overlap with decode in current pipeline mode; ensure we tag phase based on request state, not global mode.

2026-01-28 — Sofia Ivanova: Implemented budget struct + phase gating. Added counters `budget_exhausted_total` and `budget_bytes_total` tagged by phase. Decode budget defaults to 0. Need perf run with mixed-length bursts after rebase on allocator PR.

2026-02-03 — Marcus Reed: Ran perf-canary scenario locally (A100, mixed-length bursts). With prefill-only compaction budget 64MB/loop: throughput -0.2%, p99 +0.4% (within tolerance). Fragmentation ratio improved ~18% over 10 min. Attaching run ID: benchlab-2026-02-03-mlb-17.
2026-02-06 — Sofia Ivanova: Opened PR for review. Remaining: add a starvation metric (count loops where compaction wanted but phase gating blocked).
2026-02-08 — Allison Grant: Please standardize metric names to match metrics standard doc. Also add phase label enum exactly `{prefill,decode}` (no `prefill_end` etc).
2026-02-10 — Sofia Ivanova: Updated metrics naming/labels, added starvation counter. PR approved by Omar + Sean pending CI green.
2026-02-11 — Connor O'Brien: Merged into runtime-1.22 train behind feature flag. Release note will mention default decode budget = 0 for Hosted. Marking ticket done.
follow_ups: ENG-4825 — ensure eviction triggers integrate cleanly with scheduler emergency state
ENG-4828 — verify perf-canary thresholds reflect new metrics and phase gating
Add runbook note: decode compaction remains off by default; enabling requires SRE approval (runtime-1.22 canary)
